column3: The Hebrew names righteousness without explicitly supplying my plea.
The Hebrew leaves the object of finding unstated; BSB supplies evil.
The Hebrew presents calling as completed and has his utterance in the singular.
The Hebrew has lovingkindnesses in the plural.
The Hebrew does not explicitly say Your eye and names the eye’s daughter.
The Hebrew presents the assault as completed.
The Hebrew names their fat rather than callous hearts.
The Hebrew explicitly begins with our steps rather than narrating tracking us down.
The Hebrew first says his likeness, singular; BSB continues a plural comparison.
The Hebrew has a singular opponent and names his face and my soul; BSB uses them and me.
The Hebrew describes filling their belly with Your stored things; BSB names Your treasured ones and makes their sons objects of satisfying.
The Hebrew names Your likeness; BSB says Your presence.
